To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CD60 b and CD 60 c are surface-expressing molecules of human B and T lymphocyte subsets of the tonsillar system and that their expression is differentially regulated during activation and apoptosis.
CD60 b and CD 60c are surface-expressed in a differential fashion on tonsillar lymphoid cells and are involved in activation and apoptosis of these cells.
CD60 b and CD 60 c have differential effects on B cells and T cells in secondary lymphatic tissues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and functional characterization of the disialogangliotriosides of the GD3 series as novel B and T cell surface molecules.
the characterization of surface molecules of human tonsillary lymphocytes and their function in the immune response.
the characterization of the surface expression and possible functions of the O-acetylated disialo gangliosides of GD3 (GD3-OAc) on human lymphocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CD60 b and CD 60 c are involved in activation and/or apoptosis of B and T cells, respectively.
